report_profiles._comment: Epic 10 story 10.3: entry pages = sessions by GA4 landingPage. Story 10.3 Task 1 design decision: landingPage and pagePath are DISTINCT GA4 dimensions; a single runReport with BOTH produces a landingPage x pagePath cross-join (cardinality explosion). Entry pages and top pages are two independent marginal top-N lists with NO join needed (unlike GSC query>page in 10.5). So TWO report profiles, each a single-dimension top-N runReport. This profile: sessions by landingPage, orderBys sessions DESC + limit=page_top_n. row_limit is the page_top_n bound (default 50, bounded 10..200). verification_expected_rows_per_day <= 1 metric-carrier x N (upper bound, NOT exact: the long tail beyond N is dropped by design).

Epic 10 story 10.3: most-viewed pages = screen_page_views by GA4 pagePath. Second of the two page profiles (see pages_daily_landing _comment for the cross-join rationale). AI-53 honesty: the screenPageViews metric name is DECLARED per the api-schema but NOT verified live (no GA4 property connected). AC 11 / AI-13 confirms the exact metric name at the first live pass (Phase B gate); fallback if absent is sessions by pagePath (confirmed). row_limit is the page_top_n bound (default 50, bounded 10..200). verification_expected_rows_per_day <= 1 metric-carrier x N (upper bound; long tail beyond N dropped by design).

report_profiles.display_name: Acquisition Daily Report - Last Click (limited ranking)
report_profiles._comment: Epic 16 story 16.1: last-click attribution = conversions + sessions by GA4 sessionSourceMedium x sessionCampaignName. AI-53 honesty: the sessionSourceMedium / sessionCampaignName dimension names are DECLARED per the GA4 Data API doc but NOT verified live (no GA4 property connected). AC11 / AI-13 confirms the exact dimension names via the properties/{p}/metadata endpoint at the first live pass (Phase B gate). This profile carries BOTH acquisition dimensions on the same runReport row (GA4 returns them jointly for the last-click axis); the mart derives TWO MARGINAL partitions (session_source_medium, session_campaign) from it -- this is NOT a cross-join between attribution axes (the forbidden cross-join is session x first-user). Separate runReport from acquisition_daily_first_user (two marginal pulls, 10.3 pattern). dimensions lead with 'date' (manifest contract). row_limit is the top-N bound (default 50, clamped 10..200 via _get_page_top_n); orderBys conversions DESC + limit=top_n. Long tail beyond N dropped by design. verification_expected_rows_per_day <= top_n (upper bound, NOT exact). Conversion-event filter (lead_event_name) is a project preference, NOT hardcoded -- BLOCKED Phase B (default = all conversions).

report_profiles.display_name: Acquisition Daily Report - First Click (limited ranking)
report_profiles._comment: Epic 16 story 16.1: first-click attribution = conversions by GA4 firstUserSourceMedium. AI-53 honesty: firstUserSourceMedium is DECLARED per the GA4 Data API doc but NOT verified live (Phase B gate, AC11 / AI-13 confirms via metadata). Separate runReport from acquisition_daily_session (combining session x first-user dimensions in ONE runReport would produce a session x first-user cross-join -- cardinality explosion + semantic nonsense). dimensions lead with 'date'. row_limit is the top-N bound (default 50, clamped 10..200); orderBys conversions DESC + limit=top_n; long tail dropped by design. verification_expected_rows_per_day <= top_n (upper bound). Conversion-event filter (lead_event_name) BLOCKED Phase B (default = all conversions).

Epic 17 story 17.4: GA4 e-commerce transactions = conversions + purchaseRevenue by transactionId at the day grain. This is the GA4 side of the Shopify x GA4 reconciliation (doc/synthese §3.2): the transaction_reconciliation mart FULL OUTER JOINs stg_ga4_transactions_daily against stg_shopify_orders_daily by (project_id, date, transaction_id) and MEASURES the coverage rate. GRAIN DISCIPLINE (RULE ABSOLUE, lesson epic-10 + decision 15.4): the transaction grain is a JOIN KEY, NOT a breakdown partition -- per-transaction rows do NOT total the connector day, so this profile has NO fact_daily_kpi UNION block (contrast every other GA4 profile). The raw table feeds ONLY stg_ga4_transactions_daily -> transaction_reconciliation. AI-53 honesty: transactionId (GA4 Data API v1 e-commerce dimension) and conversions / purchaseRevenue metric names are DECLARED per the doc but NOT verified live (no property connected; e-commerce tracking is a property-level setup). AC / AI-13 confirms exact names via properties/{p}/metadata (Phase B gate). A lead-gen site with no e-commerce returns ZERO transaction rows -> reconciliation degrades to 'no GA4 transactions' honestly. dimensions lead with 'date' (manifest contract). PAGINATION (point dur): a day can carry more transactions than one page; unlike the acquisition/pages top-N leaderboards, transactions are a JOIN KEY -- dropping the tail would understate the coverage denominator, so the pull ORDER BY transactionId + pages on offset to completeness within a documented bound (row_limit = per-request page size, env GA4_TXN_LIMIT; _MAX_TXN_PAGES caps the offset loop; any truncation is logged, never silent). verification_expected_rows_per_day = null (transaction cardinality is unbounded per day; it is not a fixed-N leaderboard).

Story 25.9 (extends the 25.8 meta-ads reference): the catalog IS the execution contract. Any cataloged GA4 field a datastream selects is extractable at execution -- core validates the selection against api_catalog.json and passes it into pull_catalog_daily, which builds the runReport dimensions[]+metrics[] from the selection. selection_mode=catalog_driven; the metrics/dimensions listed here are the tier-core default carriers (what a None selection resolves to, pruned of realtime-incompatible minute dims). GA4 hard limits: a single runReport takes at most 10 metrics AND 9 dimensions; a wider selection CHUNKS into >1 runReport (date carried in every chunk; dimension-chunks cross metric-chunks) and the per-chunk rows MERGE on the (date, breakdown) grain key. Realtime-only minute dims (dateHourMinute/minute/nthMinute) are refused at request-build with invalid_request (catalog_sources.realtime_incompatible_fields). Lands in the dedicated long raw_ga4_catalog_daily (date, metric_name, metric_value, breakdown_dimension, breakdown_value). The legacy exact_bundle profiles + raw_ga4_standard_daily are UNTOUCHED (AD-22).

_error_map_note: Codes taken from the Google API error model (https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors, canonical google.rpc.Code -> HTTP mapping) as the GA4 Data API v1beta and the GA4 Admin API v1beta return it (https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/errors), plus the classic reason strings of the Google API Console error envelope that the Admin API still emits (https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/config/admin/v1). SHAPE THE KEYS MATCH: the JSON body { error: { code: <numeric http>, message, status: '<ENUM>', errors: [{ reason: '<reason>', domain }] } }. core.pull_errors._extract_provider_codes yields errors[].reason first, then error.status, then error.code -- so a key is written on the reason when Google publishes one and on the status enum otherwise. error.code is NEVER keyed on: it merely repeats the HTTP status and would refine nothing. WHAT THE MAP CHANGES vs the pure-HTTP classification: 403 quota reasons (quotaExceeded / rateLimitExceeded / userRateLimitExceeded) become provider_transient instead of permission_denied -- Google publishes them as 'retry with exponential backoff', and permission_denied is retryable=False, so the pure class abandoned a call that would have succeeded; 404 NOT_FOUND becomes invalid_request instead of unclassified (a property id that does not resolve is a selection drift, replaying it can never help); 409 ABORTED becomes provider_transient instead of unclassified. NO 429 KEY EXISTS BY CONSTRUCTION: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED arrives as HTTP 429 and the connector raises core.quota.RateLimitError before classify_http_error is reached (a 429 handed to the classifier raises ValueError). No auth_revoked entry: GA4 reports a revoked grant as the same 401 UNAUTHENTICATED as an expired one, with the distinction only in the free-text message -- inventing a key for it would be padding.

account_topology._comment: Story 25.5 (AC5): GA4 account hierarchy = account > property. The reporting entity (selection_level) is the PROPERTY (a GA4 runReport targets properties/{id}). discover_accounts lists what the token can reach via the GA Admin API accountSummaries.list; core owns selection/access-check/trial/backfill. Additive per AD-2: core reads levels/selection_level/discovery generically, never GA4 vocabulary.

quota._comment: Placeholder values for GA4 Data API Standard quota. GA4 quota is project-based (not per-minute points like Meta). These conservative values ensure the circuit breaker engages only on explicit 429 responses. Adjust based on observed project-level usage. See: https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/quotas

_max_provider_backfill_days_note: No max_provider_backfill_days is declared because GA4's retention is a PROPERTY SETTING the customer chooses (2 or 14 months, 26/38/50 on 360) and Google states that it 'does not affect standard aggregated reports' (https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/7667196). The Data API's DateRange publishes no earliest date (https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/rest/v1beta/DateRange). A per-property setting is not a manifest constant. Declaring a guessed window would promise a history the provider never committed to, so this module answers 'unknown' rather than a number (test_backfill_bound_is_declared_or_its_absence_is).
